headline: General Compute lands $400M loan for AI inference cloud
summary: The AI inference cloud startup secured a $400 million loan from Upper90, potentially marking the first time inference-specific chips are used as collateral.
details: General Compute, an AI inference cloud startup, has secured a $400 million loan from investment firm Upper90. This financing may be the first to use inference-specific chips as collateral, which are designed to run trained AI models efficiently.

The deal reflects a market shift towards infrastructure that supports cheaper, open-source AI models, addressing concerns about the high cost of proprietary LLMs. General Compute aims to build a specialized 'neocloud' for AI workloads.

The company's SN50 chips are optimized for inference, offering power efficiency and easier deployment compared to traditional GPU-based clouds. General Compute claims these chips will deliver 16 times faster inference speeds.
This financing strategy follows a precedent set by Crusoe, where Upper90 financed GPU purchases, demonstrating a growing acceptance of chip-backed loans in the tech industry.
Upper90 sees a significant market for inference services, especially with the rise of open-source models and companies like OpenRouter and Fireworks gaining traction.
The emergence of alternative chipmakers and models that rival top-tier offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic highlights a potential fragmentation of Nvidia's dominance in the AI hardware market.
caption:
AI inference startup General Compute secures $400M loan, potentially using inference chips as collateral for the first time.

General Compute, an AI inference cloud startup, has secured a $400 million loan from investment firm Upper90. This financing may be the first to use inference-specific chips as collateral, which are designed to run trained AI models efficiently.

The deal reflects a market shift towards infrastructure that supports cheaper, open-source AI models, addressing concerns about the high cost of proprietary LLMs. General Compute aims to build a specialized 'neocloud' for AI workloads.

The company's SN50 chips are optimized for inference, offering power efficiency and easier deployment compared to traditional GPU-based clouds. General Compute claims these chips will deliver 16 times faster inference speeds.

This financing strategy follows a precedent set by Crusoe, where Upper90 financed GPU purchases, demonstrating a growing acceptance of chip-backed loans in the tech industry.

Upper90 sees a significant market for inference services, especially with the rise of open-source models and companies like OpenRouter and Fireworks gaining traction.

The emergence of alternative chipmakers and models that rival top-tier offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic highlights a potential fragmentation of Nvidia's dominance in the AI hardware market.
